findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff removes the github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck import from sql_command.go but never adds an import for github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/expr/sql, while the body now references sql.NewInMemoryDB(), so the file does not compile. Every build of the package fails with 'undefined: sql'; CI and any downstream consumer of this module cannot compile, regardless of feature flags.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions is dead logic that returns false on every path: the 'enabled' branch returns false and the fallthrough returns false, so the feature flag FlagSqlExpressions can never enable the SQL query path. Even with the SqlExpressions feature flag enabled, ReadQuery always returns the error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' for QueryTypeSQL; the flag becomes a no-op that misleads operators into thinking enabling it does something.

[BUG] TablesList still builds and executes the 'SELECT json_serialize_sql(...)' command against duckDB := NewInMemoryDB(), whose RunCommands is a stub that unconditionally returns errors.New("not implemented"), so TablesList now always fails. Any caller of pkg/expr/sql.TablesList (an exported function) receives a 'not implemented' error for every input; the SQL-parsing logic below the RunCommands call (referenced-table extraction) is unreachable dead code.

[BUG] SQLCommand.Execute now calls db.QueryFramesInto on the stub DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go, which unconditionally returns errors.New("not implemented"), so every SQL command execution fails. Any path that reaches SQLCommand.Execute (e.g. SQL expressions issued through channels that do not go through the ReadQuery gate added in reader.go) logs 'Failed to query frames' and returns an error result to the user where the previous go-duck implementation returned real query results — a hard functional regression, not a graceful disable.

[ADVISORY] The go.mod removes scottlepp/go-duck (and its transitive h1 hashes in go.sum, e.g. araddon/dateparse) while go.work.sum simultaneously re-adds h1 entries for apache/thrift v0.20.0, JohnCGriffin/overflow, klauspost/asmfmt, and minio/asm2plan9s/c2goasm, indicating the workspace-side dependency resolution and the module-side tidy were computed against different module graphs. Whoever next runs `go mod tidy` / `go work sync` gets a churny, partially-reverted sumfile state; if the direct removal of apache/thrift from require() was hand-written rather than tidy-produced and any remaining module in the build graph still imports arrow/parquet (thrift's consumer), builds fail with a missing go.sum entry.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions returns false on both branches, so the FlagSqlExpressions feature flag is never honored and SQL expressions can never be enabled. The PR's core acceptance criterion — SQL expression queries execute when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled — is silently dropped: even a user who turns the flag on gets 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' on every QueryTypeSQL request, and the computed `enabled` variable is dead code. Worse, the variable is computed as `!h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, i.e. inverted, so a follow-up 'fix' that replaces the second `return false` with `return enabled` would enable the feature when the flag is OFF and block it when the flag is ON.

[BUG] Every method on the new DB (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) unconditionally returns errors.New("not implemented"), so pkg/expr/sql/parser.go TablesList — which previously parsed SQL via duck.NewInMemoryDB and returned real table names — now fails for every input. Existing exported functionality regresses to a hard failure: any caller of TablesList outside the new ReadQuery gate (e.g., SQL command construction/validation paths that resolve table names from the query) now receives 'not implemented' where it previously succeeded, with no migration note or fallback in the diff.

[ADVISORY] No test files exist anywhere in this diff (scanned for spec/**, test/**, __tests__/**, *_test.go, *.spec.* — none present), so the new gate branch in ReadQuery, the enableSqlExpressions helper, and the stub DB have zero verification. A regression that flips the gate logic, renames the flag constant, or drops the error return would ship silently; the changed response contract for QueryTypeSQL requests (now a 4xx-style 'not implemented' error instead of proceeding to execution) is asserted nowhere, so the next change to ReadQuery has no safety net and the inverted-flag defect above would not be caught by any test run.

[ADVISORY] The duck-specific wire format (single-quote escaping via strings.Replace plus the `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` command string) is retained against a backing engine that no longer exists, since RunCommands is now a stub that always errors. The next implementer of DB.RunCommands inherits a duck-specific command protocol embedded in parser.go that the replacement engine almost certainly will not share; this dead coupling must be unwound, and until then the escaping logic reads as load-bearing when it can never execute successfully, increasing the risk of a half-migrated implementation.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions returns false unconditionally (both the if-branch and the fall-through return false), and the `enabled` variable is computed inverted (`enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`), so the feature flag gate can never permit a SQL expression query. Every QueryTypeSQL query is rejected with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" regardless of whether FlagSqlExpressions is enabled or disabled; the flag is a silent no-op, so the PR's stated SQL analytics capability is unreachable through any configuration path.

[ADVISORY] Scope drift: the PR titled 'Advanced SQL Analytics Framework' contains no analytics implementation — it deletes the working go-duck engine and replaces it with a DB stub whose every method (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) unconditionally returns errors.New("not implemented"). The diff's net effect is the removal of SQL expression execution, not the addition of a framework; the entire SQL query path is inert, and nothing in the diff is traceable to the stated intent of building analytics capability.

[BUG] SQLCommand.Execute now calls the stub sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto, which always returns errors.New("not implemented"), so every SQL command execution fails where the previous duck-backed call could succeed. Any caller reaching Execute for a SQL command gets rsp.Error set to "not implemented" and logs 'Failed to query frames' — a guaranteed runtime failure on a path that previously executed real SQL over frames.

[BUG] TablesList now invokes the stub NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, which always returns errors.New("not implemented"), so TablesList fails on every input where the duck-backed version previously returned a table list. All callers of TablesList (SQL parse/suggestion flows) now receive 'not implemented' errors for every SQL string; the function's entire contract is silently broken while its signature and downstream parsing logic remain in place.

[ADVISORY] All logic downstream of the RunCommands call in TablesList (error handling, JSON unmarshal, flatten-based table extraction, and the jeremywohl/flatten import) is now unreachable dead code because RunCommands can only return an error. Future contributors must read and reason about parsing branches that can never execute, and the flatten dependency remains pinned for code with no live path; the next change to this file risks being built on a corpse path.

[ADVISORY] The gate returns fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") for the disabled path, conflating 'flag disabled' with 'feature not implemented', and no error or log distinguishes the two states. Operators who toggle FlagSqlExpressions off (or on — it makes no difference) see the same 'not implemented' error and cannot determine from the message or any log line whether the feature is missing or misconfigured, turning a config problem into a support debugging session.

[ADVISORY] go.work.sum churn is not traceable to the go-duck removal: unrelated modules (Azure azblob v1.3.2, google/go-replayers grpcreplay/httpreplay) are dropped while h1 hashes for the removed modules (JohnCGriffin/overflow, apache/thrift, klauspost/asmfmt, minio/asm2plan9s, minio/c2goasm) are re-added here after being deleted from go.sum. Reviewers and future bisections cannot distinguish intentional dependency work from tooling runoff; if any workspace module still requires thrift/overflow, the go.mod removal may not hold for all workspace builds.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions returns false on every code path — when the flag is disabled the first branch returns false, and when the flag is enabled execution falls through to the unconditional `return false` — so the function can never return true. Even in deployments where operators explicitly enable featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions, ReadQuery rejects every QueryTypeSQL query with the 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error; the feature flag is a no-op and the gating code gives the false impression that the flag controls behavior. The inverted binding (`enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` makes `enabled` true when the flag is OFF) means the next editor who 'fixes' the fall-through return will enable SQL for everyone, silently inverting the intended safe default.

[BUG] The new local sql.DB stub replaces the previously-working go-duck implementation, and every method (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) returns 'not implemented' unconditionally, so the entire SQL execution layer this PR is named for is inert. Every SQL expression query that previously executed via duck.NewInMemoryDB now fails at runtime: SQLCommand.Execute (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-101) stores the 'not implemented' error in rsp.Error, so existing saved panels/Alerting rules using SQL expressions break on upgrade. The 'Advanced SQL Analytics Framework' ships zero executable code — the boundary this PR establishes (a local DB abstraction standing in for go-duck) exists only as an always-failing shell.

[BUG] SQLCommand.Execute now routes every query through the stub db.QueryFramesInto, which always errors, and logs that guaranteed failure with logger.Error on each invocation. Any existing caller that reaches this path (the reader gate does not protect it — SQLCommand is constructed and executed independently of the feature-flag check in reader.go) gets a guaranteed error response where it previously got query results, and every dashboard refresh of a saved SQL expression emits a server-side error log, generating alert noise for a condition that is now the expected steady state.

[BUG] TablesList now calls the stub NewInMemoryDB whose RunCommands always returns 'not implemented', so the function can only ever return an error. Every caller of pkg/expr/sql.TablesList (used to extract referenced tables from a SQL expression) fails unconditionally; the retained string-escaping and json_serialize_sql command construction above the call is now dead code executed only to be discarded, and any feature relying on table extraction breaks with 'not implemented' regardless of feature-flag state.

[ADVISORY] The feature gate is enforced only at the ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery entry point and not inside SQLCommand.Execute itself, so the SQL execution path has two entry points but only one is gated. The author's counter-argument is that the stub errors out anyway so bypass is harmless today — that holds only until someone implements pkg/expr/sql/db.go, at which point any path that constructs SQLCommand without going through ReadQuery (tests, future alternate readers, alerting evaluation paths) executes ungated, and the flag becomes an incomplete guarantee. Putting the check at the execution boundary makes the gate hold regardless of caller.

[ADVISORY] The rejection path returns a raw fmt.Errorf('sqlExpressions is not implemented') for what is usually a normal configuration state (flag off), conflating 'feature disabled by config' with 'implementation missing', and bypasses the errutil infrastructure imported in the surrounding code. Operators who disable the flag see their existing SQL-expression dashboards fail with a message claiming the feature is unimplemented, misdirecting support/debugging toward a code-gap diagnosis when the cause is configuration; an errutil public error with a distinct reason code would let callers and users distinguish the two states.

[BUG] The PR titled 'Advanced SQL Analytics Framework' silently inverts its objective: it deletes the only working SQL execution engine (github.com/scottlepp/go-duck) and replaces every call site with a stub whose methods unconditionally return errors.New("not implemented"), so previously functional SQL expression execution and table parsing are destroyed without any replacement implementation. Every user of SQL expressions regresses: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:105 (db.QueryFramesInto) and pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23 (duckDB.RunCommands) now always fail with 'not implemented', so any dashboard or alert relying on SQL expression queries breaks at runtime the moment this ships; no code path in the diff can ever succeed, meaning the accepted intent (advanced SQL analytics) was changed to its negation without explicit human acceptance.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the feature flag state: it computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobably(FlagSqlExpressions)` (inverted), returns false in the `if enabled` branch, and then unconditionally executes a second `return false`, so FlagSqlExpressions=true and FlagSqlExpressions=false are indistinguishable. Even an operator who enables the sqlExpressions feature flag gets 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' for every SQL expression query; the flag referenced at line 195 is ships-inert (no registration, documentation, or enable path appears in this diff) and the dead `if enabled { return false }` branch makes the gate unfixable by configuration, so the intended feature-toggle contract is silently broken.

[ADVISORY] enableSqlExpressions is a three-branch construction that is logically equivalent to `return false`: the inverted boolean assignment and the dead `if enabled` branch both reduce away, leaving the feature-flag lookup as pure noise. The next engineer touching this gate must reverse-engineer three misleading branches (inversion, dead branch, duplicate return) to discover the flag has no effect; passing the deletion test, the entire function body collapses to a single `return false`, which would at least make the (currently false) intent honest and prevent the flag from being cited as evidence the feature works.

[ADVISORY] The new DB type is ships-inert scaffolding: a struct with three methods that all return 'not implemented' is kept wired into two live call sites (parser.go TablesList, sql_command.go Execute), preserving the appearance of a functioning SQL layer that can never execute. Reviewers and future contributors reading sql_command.go see a plausible execution path (NewInMemoryDB -> QueryFramesInto) and may build on it or write tests against it, only to hit a guaranteed runtime error; deleting the stub and its call sites (or erroring at construction) would make the removal explicit instead of leaving a fake implementation as a trap.

[ADVISORY] The error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' misrepresents the change: SQL expressions were implemented (via go-duck) before this diff, so the message hides a regression behind wording that suggests the feature never existed. Operators and support engineers debugging the resulting query failures will search for a missing implementation or a flag to enable, rather than recognizing that a working dependency was removed; a message stating the feature was removed/disabled (or an explicit changelog entry) would preserve intent transparency for downstream users.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions inverts the feature-flag check (`enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`) and then unconditionally returns false on every path, so the sqlExpressions gate can never pass. Operators who enable the `sqlExpressions` feature flag get no behavior change: every QueryTypeSQL expression is rejected with the misleading error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" regardless of flag state. The intended security control (feature flag gating arbitrary-SQL execution) is inert rather than correctly fail-closed, so the first person who 'fixes' the dead function to make the flag work will likely also fix the inverted check in the same stroke without reviewing either — and the gate guarding user-supplied SQL execution goes live unreviewed. Anyone reading the code will assume the flag controls the feature; it does not.

[ADVISORY] The replacement for the removed go-duck dependency is a stub whose every method (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) returns "not implemented", yet pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96 and pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23 are rewired to call it as if it were a working engine. All three call sites now fail unconditionally at runtime: SQLCommand.Execute always sets rsp.Error for any SQL expression query, and parser.TablesList always errors. Combined with the broken flag gate in reader.go, this diff ships an inert feature — three production files wired to a permanently-failing implementation. The next author must discover independently that the stub is a placeholder, not a regression; nothing in the code distinguishes 'temporarily disabled' from 'broken', so a future fix to the flag gate (finding 1) will activate a path that still always errors, converting a silent no-op into user-visible query failures.

[ADVISORY] TablesList interpolates user-controlled SQL text into a command string via fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL) with only single-quote doubling as defense, rather than parameterization — pre-existing code this diff touches and re-wires instead of removing. Quote-doubling is string-level escaping, not a parameterized query; its correctness depends on the target engine's exact literal-parsing rules (backslash handling, dollar-quoting, comment/semicolon sequences reaching json_serialize_sql's parser). rawSQL arrives from user-authored SQL expression queries, so any escaping mismatch is a SQL-injection sink into the embedded engine. Today the path is inert because RunCommands always errors, but this diff is the moment the engine swap happened and the interpolation survived it — when a real engine lands behind the stub, this unparameterized interpolation ships with it. Building the parser handoff now (parameterize or use the engine's native parse API) removes the class of risk instead of carrying it forward.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the feature flag: the `if enabled { return false }` branch and the trailing `return false` both return false, so FlagSqlExpressions has no effect and ReadQuery rejects every QueryTypeSQL query with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even when the flag is enabled. An operator who enables the sqlExpressions feature flag gets the exact same hard failure as with the flag off — the flag is a silent no-op, and any test asserting the flag-on path (e.g., reader_test.go cases for QueryTypeSQL with features enabled) would immediately fail, exposing that no test in this diff exercises the new gate at all.

[ADVISORY] All three methods of the new DB stub (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) unconditionally return errors.New("not implemented"), making the entire pkg/expr/sql package inert: sql_command.go's Execute now guarantees rsp.Error on every invocation and parser.go's TablesList always fails. Any caller that reaches these paths — including any pre-existing repo tests for TablesList or SQLCommand.Execute not touched in this diff — now hard-fails with "not implemented" instead of exercising real behavior; the swap from duck.NewInMemoryDB to this stub is a silent behavioral regression disguised as a refactor, and the shipped tables/commands/query surface cannot succeed under any configuration.

[ADVISORY] The variable `enabled` is assigned the negation of the flag check (`enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`), so its name asserts the opposite of its value, and with both branches returning false the entire function is equivalent to `return false` — the IsEnabledGlobally call and both conditionals are dead code. The next developer fixing this function (the obvious intent is `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`) is primed by the inverted variable name to write `if enabled { return true }; return false`-style logic or to keep the negation, reproducing or inverting the bug; the misleading structure makes the correct one-line fix harder to land than the wrong one.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions unconditionally returns false, so the FlagSqlExpressions feature flag is dead: the negated assignment ('enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)' is true when the flag is OFF) combined with the unconditional trailing 'return false' makes every path return false regardless of flag state. An operator who enables the sqlExpressions feature flag expects SQL expression queries to start working, but every QueryTypeSQL query still fails with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' — the flag silently has no effect, and when the real engine lands behind this gate it will remain unreachable until someone notices the constant-false body.

[ADVISORY] SQLCommand.Execute now calls a stub DB whose QueryFramesInto always returns errors.New("not implemented"), so every SQL expression execution that reaches this path fails deterministically — previously these queries executed against the removed go-duck engine. Installations with existing saved SQL expression queries (panels/alerts referencing QueryTypeSQL) regress at upgrade time: each evaluation fails with 'not implemented' and logs an error-level 'Failed to query frames' per evaluation, turning previously working dashboards into erroring panels. If this deactivation is intentional, the rollout should be verified against existing usage; as written, previously functional user work fails after deploy.

[ADVISORY] TablesList still performs quote-escaping ('' doubling) and builds the 'SELECT json_serialize_sql(...)' command string before passing it to the stub RunCommands, which can only ever return errors.New("not implemented"). The string construction and escaping are dead work on a path that can never succeed — every caller of TablesList now deterministically receives 'not implemented', so if TablesList is invoked from any flow not gated by the new reader check (e.g. query validation or SQL parsing helpers), that flow breaks; the pre-call string building should be removed until a real engine exists.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the real DuckDB dependency (github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck) and replaces it with a new pkg/expr/sql DB whose methods (including RunCommands and QueryFramesInto) unconditionally return "not implemented" (pkg/expr/sql/db.go). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TablesList still performs quote-escaping ('' doubling) and builds the 'SELECT json_serialize_sql(...)' command string before passing it to the stub RunCommands, which can only ever return errors.New("not implemented"). The string construction and escaping are dead work on a path that can never succeed — every caller of TablesList now deterministically receives 'not implemented', so if TablesList is invoked from any flow not gated by the new reader check (e.g. query validation or SQL parsing helpers), that flow breaks; the pre-call string building should be removed until a real engine exists.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now uses NewInMemoryDB() (from the new pkg/expr/sql/db.go) and then calls duckDB.RunCommands(...). But DB.RunCommands is a stub that always returns errors.New("not implemented"), so TablesList deterministically cannot succeed and will always return an error regardless of input. The finding’s point that the quote-escaping and command-string construction are dead work on this always-failing path is directly supported by the diff.
